quests.hint: Stress 'FIVE CHIL-dren' and 'WHOLE FAM-i-ly' to show the scale of her effort.
quests.explanation: Sentences admiring someone's effort over time usually stress the numbers and the scope involved.
quests.textToSpeak: The grandmother who raised five children still cooks for the whole family.

quests.hint: Stress 'EX-ACT-ly RIGHT' to express genuine appreciation.
quests.explanation: Expressions confirming someone was correct usually stress the intensifier and the key adjective together.
quests.textToSpeak: The advice my father gave me turned out to be exactly right.

quests.hint: Stress the phrasal verb 'PASSED DOWN' and 'CON-TIN-ues.'
quests.explanation: Phrasal verbs describing inheritance or legacy, like 'pass down,' stress both the verb and the particle.
quests.textToSpeak: The tradition that was passed down still continues today.

quests.hint: Stress 'WORKED' and 'NOT THE SAME' to highlight individual difference.
quests.explanation: Sentences acknowledging individual variation usually stress both the positive result and the contrasting limitation.
quests.textToSpeak: The treatment that worked for her might not work the same for everyone.

quests.hint: Stress the phrasal verb 'TRACED BACK' and 'SIM-ple AL-ler-gy.'
quests.explanation: Phrasal verbs describing investigation, like 'trace back,' stress both parts, especially when revealing a surprising cause.
quests.textToSpeak: Her symptoms were eventually traced back to a simple allergy.

quests.hint: Stress 'DI-AG-nosed' lightly, then 'ON-ly ONCE' strongly.
quests.explanation: Sentences highlighting rarity usually place the strongest stress on the limiting words, like 'only once.'
quests.textToSpeak: The specialist who diagnosed the issue had seen it only once before.

quests.hint: Stress 'DIS-COUNT-ed' and 'SOLD OUT' as the cause and the result.
quests.explanation: Sentences about quick sales usually stress both the reason for demand and the phrasal verb showing the outcome.
quests.textToSpeak: The item that was discounted sold out within an hour.

quests.hint: Stress the phrasal verb 'THROWN A-WAY' and 'MIS-take.'
quests.explanation: Passive phrasal verbs describing accidents stress both the action and the word explaining it was unintentional.
quests.textToSpeak: The receipt that I needed was thrown away by mistake.

quests.hint: Stress the idiom 'TOO GOOD TO BE TRUE' and 'RE-al.'
quests.explanation: This common idiom is pronounced as one connected rhythmic unit, contrasted here with the surprising truth.
quests.textToSpeak: The deal that looked too good to be true actually turned out to be real.

quests.hint: Stress the phrasal verb 'PATCHED UP' and 'LONG con-ver-SA-tion.'
quests.explanation: Phrasal verbs describing resolution, like 'patch up,' stress both parts to highlight the effort to reconcile.
quests.textToSpeak: The argument was eventually patched up after a long conversation.

quests.hint: Stress 'GREW UP WITH' lightly, then 'OTH-er SIDE' strongly.
quests.explanation: Sentences contrasting closeness in the past with distance now usually stress the surprising contrast.
quests.textToSpeak: The cousin who I grew up with now lives on the other side of the world.

quests.hint: Stress the phrasal verb 'HAND-ed DOWN' and 'FOUR gen-er-A-tions.'
quests.explanation: As with 'passed down,' the phrasal verb 'hand down' stresses both parts when describing a lasting tradition.
quests.textToSpeak: Our family recipe was handed down for four generations.

quests.hint: Stress the phrasal verb 'GOT O-ver' and 'TWO WEEKS.'
quests.explanation: The phrasal verb 'get over' describing recovery stresses both parts, along with the duration involved.
quests.textToSpeak: She finally got over the flu after almost two weeks.

quests.hint: Stress the phrasal verb 'PUT OFF' and 'BUS-y SCHED-ule.'
quests.explanation: Phrasal verbs describing delay, like 'put off,' stress both the verb and the particle, plus the reason for the delay.
quests.textToSpeak: His checkup was put off for months because of his busy schedule.

quests.hint: Stress the phrasal verb 'WENT A-WAY' and 'COM-PLETE-ly.'
quests.explanation: Sentences describing long-awaited relief usually stress the resolving phrasal verb and the intensifying adverb.
quests.textToSpeak: The pain that had bothered him for years finally went away completely.

quests.hint: Stress the phrasal verb 'MIXED UP' to highlight the confusion.
quests.explanation: Phrasal verbs describing mistakes, like 'mix up,' are stressed evenly across both parts to signal the confusion clearly.
quests.textToSpeak: The order that I placed online got mixed up with someone else's.

quests.hint: Stress 'PRO-CESSED' and 'FAST-er' to highlight the pleasant surprise.
quests.explanation: Sentences expressing pleasant surprise usually stress the action verb and the comparative word describing the unexpected speed.
quests.textToSpeak: The refund was processed faster than I expected.

quests.hint: Stress 'CAME WITH' lightly, then 'AC-CI-DEN-tal DAM-age' strongly.
quests.explanation: Descriptive clauses introducing a product feature flow quickly, saving the strongest stress for the key benefit.
quests.textToSpeak: The warranty that came with the product covers accidental damage.

quests.hint: Stress both phrasal verbs: 'CLEARED UP' and 'CALMED DOWN.'
quests.explanation: When two phrasal verbs appear together, both typically receive their own stress to keep the sequence of events clear.
quests.textToSpeak: The misunderstanding was cleared up once everyone calmed down.

quests.hint: Pause briefly around 'who lives abroad' to mark it as extra detail.
quests.explanation: Non-essential relative clauses, set off by commas, are usually said with a slight pause and lower stress than the main sentence.
quests.textToSpeak: My uncle, who lives abroad, visits us every other year.

quests.hint: Stress 'STRONG-er' and 'OLD-er' to highlight the parallel growth.
quests.explanation: Sentences describing parallel growth usually stress both comparative adjectives to show they happen together.
quests.textToSpeak: The bond between siblings often grows stronger as they get older.

quests.hint: Stress 'TURNED OUT' and 'OUT-DAT-ed' as the surprising discovery.
quests.explanation: Phrasal verbs like 'turn out' introducing a surprising fact are usually stressed along with the surprising detail itself.
quests.textToSpeak: The advice she was given turned out to be outdated.

quests.hint: Pause around 'which doctors called remarkable,' then stress 'LESS TIME.'
quests.explanation: Inserted relative clauses are set off with pauses, while the main comparative point keeps the strongest stress.
quests.textToSpeak: His recovery, which doctors called remarkable, took less time than expected.

quests.hint: Stress the phrasal verb 'GAVE UP' and 'AL-MOST IM-ME-DI-ate-ly.'
quests.explanation: Sentences linking a change in habit to a quick benefit usually stress both the phrasal verb and the timing adverb.
quests.textToSpeak: The habit she gave up improved her sleep almost immediately.

quests.hint: Pause around 'which had dropped overnight,' then stress 'CON-VINCED' and 'IM-ME-DI-ate-ly.'
quests.explanation: This longer sentence combines an inserted relative clause with strong stress on the resulting decision.
quests.textToSpeak: The price, which had dropped overnight, convinced me to buy it immediately.

quests.hint: Stress 'RE-DE-SIGNED' and 'RE-PEAT-ed-ly' to show the response to feedback.
quests.explanation: Sentences showing a company's response to feedback usually stress both the change made and how persistent the feedback was.
quests.textToSpeak: The packaging was redesigned after customers complained repeatedly.

quests.hint: Stress the idiom 'TURNED THINGS A-ROUND' as one connected phrase.
quests.explanation: The idiom 'turn around,' meaning to improve dramatically, is pronounced as a single rhythmic unit with even stress.
quests.textToSpeak: The store that I used to avoid has completely turned things around.

quests.hint: Stress 'MAT-ter MOST' and 'HARD-est' to highlight the central idea.
quests.explanation: This wraps up Intermediate+ by combining relative clauses, superlatives, and a meaningful, reflective message.
quests.textToSpeak: The relationships that matter most are often the ones we work hardest to maintain.

quests.hint: Pause around 'which had been shaken,' then stress 'GRAD-u-al-ly RE-BUILT.'
quests.explanation: This final example combines an inserted relative clause with a phrasal-style verb describing gradual change.
quests.textToSpeak: Her confidence, which had been shaken, was gradually rebuilt through small successes.

quests.hint: Stress 'BUILD' and 'BE-COME' to highlight the cause-and-effect relationship across time.
quests.explanation: This closing reflection ties together cause and future result, stressing both halves to leave a memorable, motivating thought.
quests.textToSpeak: The habits we build now will shape the people we become later.
